questions.question: Day 13 Practice (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): When talking about preparing breakfast for family (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The delivery executive'?

options.b: I prepared breakfast for my family this morning.
options.c: He is prepare breakfast fisily.
options.d: I am prepare breakfast family.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "I prepared breakfast for my family this morning.".

questions.question: Day 13 Vocabulary (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'circle back'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: Return to a topic later for follow-up.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'circle back' means: return to a topic later for follow-up. Example: "Let us circle back to the timeline discussion."

options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

'reach out to' means: contact someone for help or information. Example: "I will reach out to customer support tomorrow."

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 1 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: In agreement some changes if do good.
options.b: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.
options.c: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 2 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.b: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.c: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 3 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.b: Will my package be delivered by this evening?
options.c: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

questions.question:
Day 13 Translation Scenario 4 (Travel, Autos & Cabs (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.c: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.d: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.
